Hi Alice — great to meet you and Sam today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery call regarding HIPAA and PHI handling.

Recap:
- You are evaluating an LLM assistant that will ingest clinical notes and return structured recommendations. Use case will involve PHI in inference payloads.
- Primary concerns: BAA availability, where PHI may be routed/stored, audit logging, and eligible deployment modes (hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private).

What Redwood can offer (high-level):
- We can sign a BAA for customers who need HIPAA protections.
- For PHI in production, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments to ensure customer isolation, full control over network/VPC and KMS-managed keys.
- Hosted (shared) API can be used for PHI in limited pilot scenarios after legal review and a BAA, but Dedicated/Private are preferred for production.
- We provide audit logs, customer-configurable retention, and optional on-prem packaging for air-gapped needs.

Next steps:
1) I attached your vendor security questionnaire — please fill out and return.
2) Vivek (cc'd), our security/solutions engineer, will provide technical details on deployment boundaries and what we persist in logs.
3) If agreeable, we can share a BAA draft (attached) and connect legal teams.

Can you confirm: 1) intended timeline for pilot vs production, and 2) whether you expect PHI to be sent to Redwood-hosted endpoints during the pilot?

Thanks,

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>

Hi Alice — thanks for the questions. A few technical clarifications to help with your internal scoping: 

1) BAA availability: Redwood can enter into a BAA. We typically execute a BAA for Dedicated and Private customers and will evaluate hosted API BAAs on a case-by-case basis depending on data flows and customer controls. I'll ask our legal team to share the standard BAA draft.

2) PHI handling and persistence:
- In our Hosted shared API, request payloads are processed in memory and we do not use them to train models, but some telemetry/metrics may be collected. We offer options to disable telemetry and reduce retention for customers with compliance needs.
- For Dedicated and Private deployments, you control persistence policies: logs, KV cache, and model artifacts can be configured to use customer-managed KMS, and audit logs can be retained in your environment or exported to your SIEM.

3) Eligible deployment modes:
- Hosted API: possible for early pilots if de-identified data used; BAA may be possible for pilots but not recommended for long-term PHI processing.
- Dedicated (recommended): dedicated GPU pools with VPC peering/PrivateLink options, customer-managed keys, network ACLs. We can restrict egress and provide private connectivity to keep traffic inside your cloud environment.
- Private/on-prem: for customers who require air-gapped or on-prem processing, we have an on-prem package (separate engagement).

4) Auditability & evidence: we can provide SOC 2 Type II report, architecture diagrams, and optional logging export for audits. Please indicate if you need SOC 2 artifacts now and I'll arrange delivery through our secure drive.

Next steps from our side:
- I'll add a short technical appendix that describes what we persist in caches and logs by default and how to change retention.
- Marissa — please confirm legal contact so we can circulate the BAA draft and the SOC 2 artifact.

-Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Please also confirm if we can route audit logs to our Splunk instance with customer-managed keys.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: HIPAA / BAA eligibility + next steps (Acme Health)

Hi Kelly / Alice team — looping in legal/security to move this forward on our side. Answers to your two specific items below: 

- KV cache persistence: In Dedicated, the default configuration keeps KV caches in memory and ephemeral by design. We do have an option to persist caches for performance across restarts, but for HIPAA-sensitive workloads we set that to disabled and ensure caches are memory-only and wiped on instance termination. We'll include configuration guidance in the technical appendix.

- Audit logs to Splunk: Yes — we support push/export of audit logs to customer endpoints. We can configure log forwarding to your Splunk HEC endpoint over PrivateLink/VPC endpoints and you can manage encryption keys with your KMS.

Attachments: Attached is a draft BAA (Redwood_BAA_Draft.pdf) and the questionnaire you started. Please have Kelly and your legal team review the BAA; happy to take redlines.

Proposed mutual action plan: 
- Thu 05/14: Acme returns completed questionnaire (Alice/Kelly).
- Fri 05/15: Redwood provides SOC 2 artifact and technical appendix (Vivek/Neha).
- Week of 05/18: Legal-to-legal BAA review and finalize.

If that timeline looks good I'll have our legal ops send a DocuSign link once redlines are agreed.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
